steps.text: Combine bread crumbs, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper in a bowl; set aside. Whisk egg and milk together in a separate bowl. Dip dill pickle spears into the egg mixture, then into the bread crumb mixture until well-coated. Dip the pickles in the egg and bread crumb mixtures a second time so each spear is double coated. Arrange pickles in a single layer on a baking sheet. Place the baking sheet in the freezer until the breading is set, about 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep-fryer or large saucepan to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Fry the pickles in the preheated oil until light golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate.

raw_recipe.headline: Delicious Deep Fried Pickles
raw_recipe.description: These delightful appetizers are salty, tangy, and crunchy, and the recipe is easily doubled. Make them for your next party, and serve them with ranch dressing. Your guests are sure to love them.

review.reviewBody: Love these! They taste just like the ones you get at restaurants. I used pickle slices rather than spears because they make crunchier fried pickles and they're easier to eat. When you make the slices there is a lot of the bread crumb coating left over, so it might be a good idea to reduce that part of the recipe. Also, it seemed like there was an awfully lot of milk added to one egg. Less than a cup of milk would probably suffice. I'm going to try these changes next time. I served them with thousand island and it was great! I like ranch, too!

The coating is awful. Instead I used 1/2 cup milk, one egg and then around 1/4 cup flour so the pickles would stick to the bread crumbs. With this batter I also did not have to double coat it and I did not let them sit I just dunked them into the oil. Turned out delicious in the end with these changes.
The breading fell off all the pickles. Instead of milk, perhaps only eggs or a full-blown batter should be done.

love this recipe !!! but way to much milk .. the first couple pickles gets nice and coated & cooks perfect in deep fryer , but once you start coating the other half they start falling apart and the breadcrumbs gets chunky , i recommend putting half of the bread crumbs in one bowl and use that for half of the batch then discarding the remains then use the other half of breadcrumbs for the remaining pickles :) so gooood !!!!
The recipe should be cut in half for the crumb part.

i did a trial run and only had some plain bread crumbs and added some Italian seasoning and pepper, garlic powder and cayeene, I used one egg and a little bit of milk, used sliced pickles. It was tasty I think I am going to play around with the seasonings!

These were good, and if you wait for them to cool down a little the breading sticks on better. I also didn't put them in the freezer, I just coated them in the breading and put them right into the fryer - it worked fine!
No I loved it my first time
they don’t look the best but they taste the BEST!! they were so good. i did use old bay and paprika instead of cayenne pepper but still was definitely the best fried pickles i’ve ever had
Taste was great but all the coating came off while frying. Not worth all the work

I really like this recipe! Taste just like Logan Roadhouse Restaurant.

Other reviewers are correct. Too much milk in this recipe. Made with less milk and turned out great.
All the breading fell off. Very disappointed.
It's probably my own doing because I used baby Dills but I didn't get the result i was hoping for.... I will try again soon and update my review then...

Taste was good, breaking was crunchy, but it ALL fell off the pickles! The second dip in the milk/egg just washed the bread crumbs off from the first dip. Super frustrating, and once deep fried, we had pickles and pickle shaped bits of deep fried breadcrumbs - hey didn't stay together. Won't make these again.
